what_this_is: The Workshop rows for the person's files in tools/live-namespace: tool:your-files, the session the engine keeps open and reaches by calls through its one door, and tool:count-or-copy-your-file-rows, one run over the person's own database.

payload.label: Your files
payload.job: Every name of the person's files, listed, followed as it changes, read by range, written, moved, shared and released, for an AI or a device's folder, through the engine's one door
payload.description: The person's files (tools/live-namespace) as a session the engine keeps open and reaches only by calls: tools:run at @tools {tool: "tool:your-files", call: {name, arguments}} sends one MCP tools/call to the account's one session of this row, which the first call starts (trillion-rust src/tool_runs/tools/sessions.rs `call`); each call is answered on its own, so a list_changes that waits holds back no read. `name` is an operation of mcp-tools.json: list_files, list_changes, show_item, read_file_span, write_file, write_file_start, write_file_piece, write_file_finish, move_names, set_aside, put_back, make_folder, set_pin_rule, thumbnail, bounds, this_computer and the rest. The answer is {tool, result} with the operation's answer in result.structuredContent; a refusal is result.isError with {code, outcome}. The run opens no port. Its names are rows in the person's own Postgres database (own-rows-postgres-connection, reached on the loopback port the computer reports as own-rows-postgres); its bytes are the person's own files-store connection, each field mounted on the descriptor settings.json `attached` names and never printed. The program is the live-namespace this computer keeps among its program folders.

output_schema.description: A call answers {tool, result: {structuredContent, content, isError}} or {tool, error}; the session's start answers its state.

provenance.source: Trillion-X/trillion-rust src/account_files at 5fbc2ff4b1 (moved into tools/live-namespace), over its own rows in SQL (src/store)

payload.label: Count or copy the rows of your files
payload.job: Count the rows of each table of the person's files index, or copy an archive's index tables into the person's own database
payload.description: Runs tools/live-namespace once over the person's own Postgres database (own-rows-postgres-connection on descriptor 8, reached on the loopback port the computer reports as own-rows-postgres). Mode `counts` answers each names-index table and how many rows it holds, and only reads. Mode `copy-archive` copies the ns_* tables of the SQLite archive at `from` (a path on this computer, opened read-only) into the database and answers each table's rows. Neither reaches the byte store.

mode.description: counts: rows per table, only reads. copy-archive: copy the archive at `from` in.

from.description: copy-archive only: the absolute path of the archive SQLite file on this computer.

output_schema.description: One line per table on stdout: the table and its rows.

provenance.source: Trillion-X/trillion-rust src/account_files at 5fbc2ff4b1 (moved into tools/live-namespace), over its own rows in SQL (src/store)
